correctness.rationale: For transient states x,y, directed rates a=q_xo>0, b=q_xy, c=q_yo, d=q_yx, exact backward equations yield (r+b+c+d)/(ar+a(c+d)+bc), derivative b(c-a)/denominator^2 and hence no strict interior minimizer even with directed edges and traps at r=0. Independently solving the 3x3 four-state reset equations yields rational M=(r²+7r+9)/(r²+8r+7), derivative (r²-4r-23)/(denom²), one positive zero 2+3√3, negative then positive; its value is 2/3+√3/6. For any graph with h(v)<=a, the killing-intensity Feynman–Kac representation bounds survival below by e^-at and hence mean >=1/a. The finite-state resolvent has f(r)=a/r+O(r^-2), so renewal M(r)=(1-f(r))/(r f(r)) tends to 1/a. The independent checker verified the algebra and derivative. No result claims homogeneous equal-weight nearest-target finite optimum.
